assessments.reasoning: The static rule at jls-10.1-210 explicitly excludes length from the array type. The array type notation in jls-10.1-110 preserves nesting depth, and jls-10.2-310 permits a variable of a given array type to refer to arrays with different lengths.

challenge.method: Read the precise exclusion and the bracket-depth provision in §10.1 alongside the assignment provision in §10.2. On Temurin 21.0.12.1+1 for Windows, compared class identity across lengths and ragged subarrays and varied nesting depth and primitive component type as controls.
challenge.results: Arrays of lengths zero and one shared the same int[] class. The two int[] subarrays in a ragged int[][] also shared a class despite lengths zero and three. The int[][] and short[] controls had distinct classes.

limitations: Array type can distinguish component types and nesting depths. Length remains an object property.
